newsitem.title: USA: NHL ICE HOCKEY-LATE LINDROS GOAL GIVE FLYERS 3-1 SERIES LEAD.
newsitem.headline: NHL ICE HOCKEY-LATE LINDROS GOAL GIVE FLYERS 3-1 SERIES LEAD.

text.p: Eric Lindros scored a power-play goal with 6.8 seconds left to give the Philadelphia Flyers a 3-2 victory Friday, foiling a valiant attempt by the battered, undermanned New York Rangers to even the NHL Eastern Conference finals.

With the game apparently headed for overtime, Lindros snapped a wicked backhander from the left faceoff circle that Rangers goaltender Mike Richter never had a chance to stop, giving Philadelphia a commanding three games to one lead in the best-of-seven series.
"That was quite an ending to a pretty wide-open game," said Philadelphia coach Terry Murray, whose team can advance to the Stanley Cup championship round with a win at home Sunday.
Lindros, who scored three goals in the previous game, had been held fairly well in check by the Rangers Friday. But the huge Flyers captain came through for his team when it counted most.

The Rangers had cleared the puck out of their zone with time running out, but the Flyers brought it right back. Rod Brind'Amour left the puck for John LeClair, who made a brilliant backhanded pass across the slot to set up Lindros's game-winner.

"That was a pretty special goal ... a tremendous shot taken on the backhand," said Murray, pointing out that most players in that position on the ice would have tried to switch to a forehand shot, which might have given Richter or the Rangers defencemen time to get back into position.
The ending was especially disheartening for the Rangers, who had so many players missing from the lineup or playing hurt that it was a wonder they could compete at all.

Yet, they twice tied the game in a thrilling third period, the second time with 2:08 left on a goal by Brian Leetch that was set up by Wayne Gretzky -- two leading members of New York's corps of walking wounded.
"The guys who were left playing played as hard as they could," said New York coach Colin Campbell.

With the game tied 2-2 and 1:35 left in regulation, New York defenceman Jeff Beukeboom hit LeClair in the face with his stick, drawing blood and taking a penalty that could well haunt him throughout the off-season.
"It was a bitter way to lose and a bitter pill to swallow, but it's a tough tournament," Campbell said.
Gretzky -- who has 10 post-season goals -- was hurt during the second period when he was slashed across the forearm by Eric Desjardins.
"Wayne Gretzky played the rest of the game but he was playing with one arm. He couldn't shoot," complained Campbell.
The Flyers grabbed a 1-0 lead on a goal by Mikael Renberg at 7:08 of the opening period.
Dale Hawerchuck banged the puck off the backboard and it came right to Renberg at the Rangers' left goalpost. As two New York players converged on him, Renberg managed to stuff the puck into the net.
He was rewarded for his effort by getting punched in the face by Beukeboom.

The Rangers were lucky to come out of the first period down by just one. About six minutes into the game on a Flyers power play, LeClair ripped a shot that beat Richter but hit off the inside of the left post, buzzed along the goal line and ticked off the right post.
With just over a minute left in the first, the Flyers had another golden opportunity, but Richter made two saves in rapid succession on point-blank shots by Hawerchuck, who was alone in front.
Richter finished with 39 saves, many of them remarkably acrobatic stops.
Veteran Flyers goalie Ron Hextall turned in his second successive winning performance, stopping 31 shots.
There were no goals in the middle period but plenty of big saves and close calls by both teams.
Early in the second, Leetch, who could barely shoot because of an injury, managed to bang one off the crossbar. About three minutes later, Richter robbed Brind'Amour right in front.
A flurry of penalties midway through the period gave the Rangers a 4-on-3 and then a 5-on-3 advantage, but Hextall and the Flyers penalty killers thwarted New York.
"The special teams did a great job," Murray said. "Killing off that four-on-three in the second period was huge for us."
The Rangers were down a man to start the third when Esa Tikkanen scored the best goal of the series to knot the score 1-1 at 1:41, whipping a previously subdued crowd into a frenzy.
He made a brilliant end-to-end rush, using nifty stickhandling to control the puck and split a pair of Flyers defenceman before poking the puck past Hextall while falling to the ice.
The rest of the game was played at fever pitch by both clubs.
With 3:13 left, Philadelphia's John Druce banged home a rebound of his own shot for a short-handed goal and a 2-1 lead that temporarily silenced the crowd.

But just 65 seconds later, Gretzky got a loose puck in his office -- behind the opposition net -- and found Leetch streaking unchecked toward the Flyers goal. Leetch buried the puck, knotting the score until Lindros's stunning game winner.
"They played hard," said Lindros. "But we got the last break."
